title: AN/MS standard aircraft hardware reference
sources: FAA-H-8083-30A, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook - General

provenanceKey.C: CONFIRMED - stated in the cited FAA sources
provenanceKey.A: ASSUMPTION - general knowledge, explicitly NOT found in those sources
provenanceKey.X: CONFLICTED - sources disagree; do not rely on

criticalWarnings.title: The AN dash number means two different things
criticalWarnings.detail: For BOLTS the dash number is the shank DIAMETER in sixteenths of an inch. For FLUID FITTINGS the dash number is the TUBE OUTSIDE DIAMETER in sixteenths of an inch. They are unrelated systems that share a naming convention.
criticalWarnings.consequence: An 'AN-4' bolt and an 'AN-4' fitting do not share a thread and are not interchangeable in any sense. Torque tables for one must never be applied to the other.

criticalWarnings.title: Fluid fitting thread sizes are absent from the FAA sources, but are now resolved externally
criticalWarnings.detail: AC 43.13-1B and FAA-H-8083-30A list 7/16-20 and 9/16-18 in generic thread tables but never map them to AN-4 or AN-6 fittings. That gap is real and still true of those documents. The mapping has since been resolved against two independent industry sources and is recorded in fluidFittings.threadTable; the governing standards are named in fluidFittings.standards. Supersedes the earlier FITTING-THREAD-UNVERIFIED warning.

bolts.family: AN3 - AN20 standard hex head bolt
bolts.purpose: All-purpose structural fastener for tension or shear where a light drive fit is acceptable.

diameterCode.rule: dash number = nominal diameter in SIXTEENTHS of an inch

lengthCode.rule: length designated in EIGHTHS of an inch

headMarkings.material: special purpose / high strength, heat treated

prohibitions.rule: Steel bolts smaller than No. 10-32 must not be used in primary structure
Aluminium alloy bolts smaller than 1/4 inch must not be used in primary structure
Aluminium alloy bolts and nuts must not be used where frequent removal for inspection or maintenance is required
Aluminium alloy bolts are PROHIBITED on seaplanes (dissimilar metal galvanic corrosion)
Aluminium alloy bolts are permitted with cadmium-plated steel bolts loaded in shear on landplanes

gripRules.rule: Grip length is the thickness of the material the bolt is designed to hold
Washers may shim the grip to a standard size, but total washer stack must NOT exceed 1/8 inch
Measure the physical bolt before installation rather than relying on the parts manual

nuts.name: castle nut
nuts.locking: cotter pin or safety wire through castellations
nuts.usedWith: drilled-shank hex bolts, clevis bolts, drilled-head bolts, studs

nuts.name: plain nut
nuts.locking: none - requires auxiliary locking device (checknut or safety wire)
nuts.note: Structural use on aircraft is highly limited

nuts.name: self-locking nut, regular height
restrictions: Never use on any joint where the nut or bolt is subject to rotation
Not on turbine engines where a loose nut could enter the air intake
Not on access panels routinely opened before or after flight
Repeated removal degrades prevailing torque - replace when below minimum

reusedSelfLockingNutMinPrevailingTorque.note: Minimum prevailing torque a reused self-locking nut must still exhibit. Below this, discard.

washers.name: plain flat washer
uses: smooth bearing surface under a hex nut
shim to obtain proper grip length
position a castellated nut relative to the drilled cotter-pin hole

rules.rule: Always use a plain washer under a lockwasher to prevent gouging the bearing surface
Cadmium-plated steel washers required under steel bolt heads and nuts on aluminium alloy or magnesium structure, to prevent galvanic corrosion

washers.name: large-diameter plain washer
uses: wooden structure, under bolt heads and nuts, to prevent crushing wood fibres
bonding stud buildups, to hold tinned copper braid and lugs flush to the airframe

designations.use: where nonmagnetic properties or superior corrosion resistance are required

rules.rule: NEVER reuse a cotter pin - always install new
Select the largest diameter pin that fits the bolt shank hole and the castellation slots
Install clevis pins head up or forward, so gravity retains the pin if the cotter pin fails

fluidFittings.note: See criticalWarnings.AN-DASH-COLLISION before using anything in this section alongside the bolt data.

sizing.rule: dash number = tube OUTSIDE DIAMETER in sixteenths of an inch

flareAngleDeg.warning: 45 degree automotive flaring tools are PROHIBITED - they cause misfit, stress and system failure

standards.note: AN fittings were originally built to MIL-F-5509. They are now controlled under SAE Aerospace Standards. The 37 degree flare form itself is SAE J514.

threadTable.note: Dash size to male thread. Corroborated by two independent sources on 2026-07-31 (Pegasus Auto Racing AN reference and the AN thread standards summary). These threads are NOT in AC 43.13-1B or FAA-H-8083-30A, which is why this table exists. See criticalWarnings.AN-DASH-COLLISION before using alongside the bolt table - an AN-4 BOLT is 1/4-28, an AN-4 FITTING is 7/16-20.
threadTable.threadSeriesCaveat: Listed as SAE/UNF sizes. Neither consulted source states whether the military UNJF variant (controlled root radius) applies to a given part number; treat the series designation as unconfirmed even though the size is confirmed.

doubleFlareRule.rule: Double flare mandatory on soft aluminium alloy tubing 3/8 inch OD and under

assemblyRules.rule: Slip the AN818 nut and AN819 sleeve onto the tube BEFORE flaring
Lubricate the flare faces and threads with clean hydraulic fluid only
NEVER apply thread compound to the flare face - it destroys the metal-to-metal seal
Never use nut torque to pull a misaligned line into place
Any crack or deformity in a flare is cause for immediate rejection

clamps.name: cushioned loop clamp (Adel)
clamps.use: primary support for wire bundles, coax and plumbing lines
clamps.construction: metal band with elastomeric or synthetic rubber cushion liner

rules.rule: Cushioned clamps required wherever vibration exists; plain clamps only where there is none
Bonded cushioned clamps MANDATORY on metal hydraulic, fuel or oil lines; unbonded clamps are for electrical wiring ONLY
Teflon cushion required where Skydrol, hydraulic fluid or fuel exposure is expected - but Teflon is less resilient and damps vibration worse than rubber
Mounting bolt angular offset max 45 degrees from the loop axis
Mount attachment hardware ABOVE the clamp wherever practicable, so line weight cannot rotate it into chafing
Back of the clamp should rest against a structural member where practical

clamps.name: bare metal bonding clamp
clamps.use: electrical bonding of metallic conduit or tube structure - NOT a fluid line clamp

rules.rule: Only AN735-6 and larger permitted for instrument panel bonding
Cadmium-plated steel clamp, nut and washers

clamps.name: plain uncushioned loop clamp
clamps.use: securing rigid plumbing or bundles in non-vibration zones where metal-to-metal contact is acceptable

clamps.name: worm-drive / radial hose clamp
clamps.conflictNote: One source quoted radial (28 TPI) ~25 in-lb and worm screw (10 TPI) ~15 in-lb, and recommended re-torque checks for several days to allow for cold flow. Two other sources state AN737 is entirely absent from their text. Values are NOT to be relied on without a real AN737 drawing.

lineSupport.conflictWarning: Two different rigid-line support spacing tables exist in the FAA literature and they DISAGREE. Both are recorded. AC 43.13-1B bands by OD; the AMT Handbook splits by material. Known examiner trap.

flexibleHose.rule: Support flexible hose at least every 24 inches; 18 inches preferred
Install with 5 to 8 percent slack - never stretched tight between fittings
Hose must run straight for at least TWO HOSE DIAMETERS from the end of the metal fitting before any bend or support clamp
Clamp to prevent twisting - a twisted pressurised hose torsionally loads its fittings

bonding.rule: Metallic fuel lines bonded to structure at EVERY clamp point
DC resistance 1 ohm or less to main structure for fuel line supports and connections
Remove paint/anodise between clamp and tube over the clamp width and at least 1 inch of circumference; re-prime after bonding check
Apply Alodine conversion coating to bare aluminium within 24 hours of finish removal
Never ground or bond electrical wires directly to magnesium parts

knownGaps.status: NOT present in AC 43.13-1B Ch.7 or FAA-H-8083-30A per query

knownGaps.status: NOT resolved - size is confirmed, series is not. See fluidFittings.threadTable.threadSeriesCaveat
NOT present - see clamps AN737 conflictNote
